writeup.headline: NetApp rates Buy on accelerating growth, strong margins and net cash, held back by a full valuation.
writeup.thesis: NetApp scores 70, a Buy, driven by strong growth, quality, balance sheet and trend scores. Latest-quarter revenue growth of 29.9% year on year, with growth sped up by 17.4 pp from the previous quarter, sits alongside TTM revenue growth of 12.2%, a 25.0% operating margin, a 22.3% FCF margin and diluted share count down 1.5% year on year. The balance sheet is net cash with cash covering debt 1.44 times, and the shares are price 53.3% above its 200-day average and 4.8% below its 52-week high. Valuation is the main drag at a score of 28: in absolute terms the stock trades at 6.0x sales, 27.1x FCF and 23.6x EV/EBIT, with an FCF yield 1.3 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and it is expensive against its own history, more expensive than at 60 of the last 61 month-ends on each multiple. News is roughly neutral, with positive analyst actions offset by small director sales.
key_risks: Valuation is expensive against its own history and the FCF yield sits below the 10-year Treasury yield, leaving little room for disappointment.
After a 77.5% gain from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, the shares could pull back sharply if momentum fades.
Q2 results due 2026-12-01 need to confirm the raised FY2027 guidance and the recent growth acceleration.
Barclays downgraded on valuation, and two directors sold shares with no insider buying.
what_would_change: A drop of 6 points in the score would move the rating to Hold, for example from a weaker trend score or a slowdown in growth at Q2 results.
A gain of 10 points would reach Strong Buy, most plausibly through a better valuation score if earnings grow faster than the share price.
A guidance cut or margin compression would hit the growth and quality scores, which together carry 40% of the weight.
